skill.name: azure-kubernetes
skill.description: Plan and configure Azure Kubernetes Service clusters, including SKU choice, networking, security, observability, scaling, upgrades, and cost controls.
skill.summary: Design production-ready AKS clusters and migration choices with Azure best practices.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Kubernetes field names, documentation URLs, and safety examples. Confirmed risks relate to Azure CLI or MCP actions against live cloud resources, AKS credential permissions, temporary export of cluster manifests, and RBAC grant guidance. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Azure CLI and MCP operations can read or change live AKS resources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before live Azure actions, show the exact command or tool call, and prefer read-only operations when possible.

remediation.issue: The MCP integration reference includes an Azure RBAC role assignment command.
remediation.suggestion: Do not auto-run role assignment commands. Present them as manual steps, require explicit approval, and use least-privilege scope.

remediation.issue: Fallback guidance writes cluster inventory files to /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-approved restricted workspace path or in-memory processing, and redact sensitive workload fields before saving.

remediation.issue: Live assessment requires sensitive AKS credential-related permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Document why listClusterUserCredential/action is needed and offer offline manifest validation when users cannot grant that permission.

content.value_statement: AKS planning involves early choices that affect security, networking, scale, and cost. This skill guides cluster design, migration readiness, and operational decisions with Azure-specific checks.
actual_capabilities: Plan AKS Automatic or Standard cluster configurations.
Compare Azure CNI Overlay, Cilium, ingress, and egress options.
Recommend identity, secrets, policy, observability, upgrade, and cost controls.
Assess AKS Automatic readiness for workloads and cluster configuration.
Guide pod rightsizing, VPA, autoscaler, and Spot node pool decisions.
Use Azure MCP or Azure CLI guidance when the user authorizes live checks.
limitations: It cannot guarantee current Azure regional quotas or service availability.
Live cluster checks require configured Azure credentials and appropriate permissions.
It provides guidance; users must approve commands and infrastructure changes.
Bundled readiness constraints may lag newer AKS Automatic policy versions.

use_cases.title: Design New AKS Clusters
use_cases.description: Select SKU, networking, identity, observability, and upgrade settings before provisioning production clusters.

use_cases.title: Prepare AKS Automatic Migration
use_cases.description: Check workloads and cluster settings against AKS Automatic compatibility rules before migration planning.

use_cases.title: Optimize Cluster Cost and Scale
use_cases.description: Review rightsizing, autoscaler, VPA, and Spot node pool choices for resilient cost reduction.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an AKS SKU
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose AKS Automatic or AKS Standard for a production web application. Ask only for missing requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Networking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design AKS networking for a private production cluster with controlled egress, ingress, and pod IP planning.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Automatic Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my Kubernetes manifests for AKS Automatic compatibility and list blockers, required changes, and safe fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Cost and Reliability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review an AKS cluster for rightsizing, autoscaler tuning, VPA usage, Spot pools, and upgrade reliability tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: I need an AKS cluster for a customer-facing API in two regions.
output: Recommended SKU: AKS Automatic unless custom node pool control is required.
Day-0 decisions: private API access, Azure CNI Overlay, Cilium, controlled egress, and zone-aware deployment.
Security baseline: Entra ID, Workload Identity, Key Vault CSI, Azure Policy, and Defender for Containers.

output_examples.input: Can this workload move to AKS Automatic?
output: Readiness summary: separate incompatible items, required manifest changes, and informational warnings.
Fix plan: show deterministic YAML diffs first and request approval before writing files.
Next step: rerun validation after fixes and review remaining cluster configuration decisions.

output_examples.input: How can I lower AKS costs without hurting production reliability?
output: Review CPU and memory requests against observed usage before changing node pools.
Use autoscaler profiles carefully and keep production minimums aligned with availability needs.
Use Spot pools only for workloads that tolerate interruption and have safe fallback capacity.

best_practices: State whether commands may read or change Azure resources before running them.
Confirm subscription, resource group, cluster name, and region with the user.
Treat Day-0 networking decisions as design choices that may require recreation.
anti_patterns: Do not run az aks update or role assignment commands without explicit approval.
Do not ask users to paste secrets, kubeconfigs, tokens, or subscription identifiers.
Do not assume Spot pools, VPA Auto mode, or autoscaler settings fit every workload.

faq.question: Does this skill create AKS clusters automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide cluster creation, but users should approve every command before Azure resources are changed.

faq.question: Can it assess an existing cluster?
faq.answer: Yes. Live assessment requires Azure MCP or Azure CLI access with suitable cluster permissions.

faq.question: Does it handle AKS Automatic migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes readiness checks, blocker grouping, and fix guidance for AKS Automatic compatibility.

faq.question: Can it optimize AKS costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers rightsizing, VPA recommendations, autoscaler settings, and Spot node pool tradeoffs.

faq.question: Will it expose secrets?
faq.answer: The skill instructs agents not to request or output secrets, tokens, kubeconfigs, or connection strings.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
